help.paragraph: {mark} Products that are created within the factory. Products are first used to fulfil recipes internally, and any surplus is then available for Export. E.g. if you add 200 Iron Rods and also 100 Screws, you'd have 100 surplus Rods remaining used as an Export (and the Screws as a end product).
help.paragraph-1: Products that are created within the factory. Products are first used to fulfil recipes internally, and any surplus is then available for Export. E.g. if you add 200 Iron Rods and also 100 Screws, you'd have 100 surplus Rods remaining used as an Export (and the Screws as a end product).
help.paragraph-2: An {green} product is one that is used to produce other products. The surplus of which can also be used as an export.
help.internal: An {internal} product is one that is used to produce other products. The surplus of which can also be used as an export.
help.noDemand: An {noDemand} product means the product is not used internally nor exported. It is suggested you delete this.

import.help: Imports are the resources needed to produce the factory's products and ensure its satisfaction. To set up imports, you select another factory and choose one of its outputs. This creates a "request" for that output. The selected factory must fulfill this request, and you'll be notified if it cannot meet the demand. All available outputs are listed in the Outputs section of the factory you choose.

selection.error: There are no factories available to import the current product selection
selection.rawOnly: This factory is only using raw resources and requires no imports.
selection.noImport: There are no factories that have exports available to supply this factory.

rawResources.help: Raw resources (e.g. Iron Ore) aren't defined as imports. It is assumed you'll supply them sufficiently. It seemed a little pointless to force you to make a factory to input it directly into a factory.

satisfaction.empty: Awaiting product selection or requirements outside of Raw Resources.
satisfaction.help: Amount of the item that is available after internal production needs and other export requests are taken into account. This amount is available for other factories to import.
satisfaction.fixManuallyTooltip:
You have multiple Generator groups for this waste. Since the planner cannot read your mind, we don't know which group to fix.
Please either fix manually or reduce to one Generator & Fuel group.
satisfaction.correctManuallyTooltip:
This item is a byproduct, currently the planner does not know how to scale byproducts correctly
as there could be a number of ways to do it that the user may not want.
Please scale it manually.
satisfaction.fixImportTooltip:
There are multiple Imports for this Item. The planner doesn't know which one you would want to be fixed.
Please correct manually by using the Satisfy buttons in the Imports section.

breakdown.rawTooltip: Raw Items e.g. Iron Ore are always satisfied. Expand the Satisfaction Breakdowns or look at the Imports section for details of how much is needed

tasks.label: New Task
tasks.limitMessage: You are only allowed up to 50 tasks.

syncStatus.clickTooltip: Mark as in sync with game
syncStatus.textTooltip:
Game Sync is when you have implemented the factory inside the game.
When it drops out of sync, there are changes that you need to implement.
When a factory's products are changed, the factory will be out of sync, or if you set it manually.

resources.info: Shows the amount of raw resources consumed by all your factories.

buildings.info: Shows the amount buildings of each type in all your factories.

power.info: Shows world level power consumption and generation data.

itemsDifference.info: Shows the amount of surplus or deficit of items you have in your factory. These are items that either need to be produced more (in red), or items that can be stored or sunk (in green)!

items.info: Shows all the items produced by all your factories.

summary.help: Showing an overview of each factory with the name, buildings and their production.
